ownership_reason: Each archiver's stream is created by exactly one step of the chain, and only the gold creates tar and cpio streams; hops 2, 3 and 4 pass the factory's entry encoding on unchanged, as their javadoc says, and hop 1 applies it only to the zip and jar streams it creates itself. The gold's javadoc promises a stream 'with the entry encoding of an archive stream factory', the encoding 'as ArchiveStreamFactory#getEntryEncoding() returns it'; for a factory, an absent entry encoding means the archiver default (getEntryEncoding: 'or null for the archiver default'; setEntryEncoding: 'Use null for the archiver default'), and the cpio archiver default is ASCII (CpioArchiveOutputStream(OutputStream): 'using ASCII encoding for file names'). The variant gold always uses the encoding constructor, so a factory without an entry encoding gets a cpio stream with the platform's default instead. A cpio stream's file-name encoding is fixed by its constructor, so no caller can recover it after the gold returns. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling factory methods ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream) and createArchiveInputStream(InputStream) create the cpio (and zip, jar, arj, dump) stream with the archiver's own default constructor when the entry encoding is null; ArchiveStreamFactoryTest testEncodingInputStream and testEncodingInputStreamAutodetect (cpio with a default factory expects US-ASCII) pass, as do cantWrite7zToStream through the chain and ExceptionMessageTest testMessageWhenOutputStreamIsNull.
